issue.title: test: cover push-path auth failure (same class as the fixed CVE)
issue.body:
## Summary
The known historical CVE in this repo was credential-forwarding on push (\`PushRemoteDataSpecReferrer\`). Yet every automated auth test that runs in CI exercised only the **fetch** path - the **push** credential path was covered solely by an env-gated integration test that's skipped in CI, and even that only ever used valid credentials, never asserted an auth failure. A regression of the exact CVE class would not have been caught by anything automated.

Adds an httptest-based push test mirroring the existing fetch tests (\`TestFetchVolumeFromRemote_Unauthorized\`/\`_Forbidden\`): mock registry returns 401 + \`WWW-Authenticate\` on every non-ping request, asserts \`errors.Is(err, ErrAuth)\`, and additionally asserts an \`Authorization\` header was actually sent — proving credentials were forwarded to the push path, not just that push failed for some unrelated reason.

Part of the cross-repo Go CI guardrail initiative, Bundle 5 (domain profile) extension.

Addresses the push-auth item of #11 (one of several; push-partial-failure, a CI smoke-cycle wiring, and skip-tracking annotations remain open there).

## Test plan
- [x] \`go test -run TestPushLocalToRemote_Unauthorized -race -count=10\` — clean
- [x] \`go test -race ./...\` — full suite passes
- [x] \`gofmt -l\` / \`go vet\` clean

body: **Priority: Medium.** The highest-risk item (push-path auth, matching the exact fixed-CVE class) is done in #12, including a test that was verified to actually distinguish the vulnerable oras-go version from the fixed one. What's left - push partial-failure handling, wiring a real registry smoke cycle into CI, skip-tracking annotations, and confirming the in-fetch chunk-digest branch isn't shadowed - are all secondary hardening, not live regression risk on the path that had a real CVE history.

**Follow-up on the "Realistic push/pull smoke cycle in CI" item**: this can be done at effectively zero additional cost. CI already runs on `ubuntu-latest` (GitHub-hosted), which has Docker built in and supports Actions `services:` containers natively — a `registry:2` service container runs inside the same job allocation, so it doesn't add billed runner time beyond the few seconds it takes to start plus however long the actual push/pull round-trip takes.

Suggested shape:

```yaml
services:
  registry:
    image: registry:2
    ports:
      - 5000:5000
```

Then point `scripts/sorictl-registry-smoke.sh` (or a new CI-only invocation of `integration_registry_test.go`'s push+resolve+fetch cycle) at `localhost:5000` with `PlainHTTP: true`. This gets a real push/pull round-trip against an actual OCI registry implementation into every PR, without needing live Harbor/GHCR/ECR credentials — those stay as the existing env-gated integration tests for the parts that specifically need a real cloud registry (auth flows, cross-account behavior, etc.).

issue.title: [CURRENT CI GAP] Shared-filesystem fixture smoke remains environment-gated and non-visible in CI
issue.body:
## CURRENT CENTRAL DISPOSITION — 2026-09-10

**Status: OPEN / GENUINE ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT TEST VISIBILITY GAP.**

The original finding remains materially correct, with one current-code correction: the smoke tests now accept either `TORI_SHARED_FIXTURE_ROOT` **or** the fallback `TORI_NAS_FIXTURE_ROOT`. If neither is set, the suite still skips.

Current `block/shared_fs_fixture_smoke_test.go` follows the pattern:

```go
root := os.Getenv("TORI_SHARED_FIXTURE_ROOT")
if root == "" {
    root = os.Getenv("TORI_NAS_FIXTURE_ROOT")
}
if root == "" {
    t.Skip("TORI_SHARED_FIXTURE_ROOT is not set")
}
```

Current `.github/workflows` contains only `codeql.yml`, `core-ci.yml`, and `security-observe.yml`. `core-ci.yml` runs `make test-core`; it does not provision a shared/NAS fixture root or run a dedicated shared-filesystem fixture job.

So a green ordinary CI run does **not** prove that the shared-filesystem fixture smoke actually executed.

## Why this matters

This is not an argument that production NAS infrastructure must be reachable from every PR. The gap is that environment-dependent coverage exists but its execution/non-execution is not represented as an explicit CI fact. A future regression in the shared-filesystem path can remain invisible if every run simply skips.

This is especially important because the fixture suite exercises semantics such as:

- paired FASTQ grouping and missing-role behavior;
- duplicate-role fail-closed handling;
- BAM/BAI and CRAM/CRAI role/pairing probes;
- shared-filesystem input behavior that ordinary unit tests do not prove end-to-end.

## Current required outcome

Choose a bounded verification strategy; do not hard-code a specific NAS product into Tori semantics.

Acceptable shapes include:

1. **Scheduled/manual real-fixture lane** on an authorized runner with the required mount, with a hard assertion that the suite actually ran; or
2. **CI-visible skip/evidence reporting** in ordinary CI plus a separately required/observed real-fixture lane; or
3. a reproducible substitute fixture environment if it proves the same required filesystem semantics without depending on the production NAS.

Whatever mechanism is chosen, the semantic contract must remain provider-neutral: Tori needs evidence that its supported shared-filesystem profile was exercised, not evidence that one named NAS vendor was used.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CI/verification output distinguishes **executed and passed** from **not executed because shared fixture environment was unavailable**.
- [ ] At least one reproducible lane actually runs the shared-filesystem fixture suite on the supported deployment profile.
- [ ] The lane fails if the suite unexpectedly all-skips when it was expected to run.
- [ ] Fixture-root configuration is explicit and does not leak environment-specific paths into canonical Tori semantics.
- [ ] The verification artifact records the tested profile/environment sufficiently to interpret the result later.
- [ ] Ordinary PR CI is not falsely described as proving shared-filesystem behavior when that lane did not execute.

## Non-goals

- Do not require the production NAS in every GitHub-hosted PR job.
- Do not make NAS vendor/path names part of Tori's semantic model.
- Do not reopen Tori grouping/duplicate semantics from this issue.
- Do not fold the historical Fixture D/DB Skipf cleanup from #23 into this issue.

Related: #23 tracks stale/historical skip handling and unexpected real-SQLite setup skips.

**Implementation gate:** this is an operability/test-evidence gap, not an immediate code authorization. Select the supported execution environment and fresh tori repo slot before modifying CI.

issue.title: test: isolate per-chunk digest-mismatch branch, cover push partial-failure
issue.body:
## Summary
Two remaining items from #11:

1. **`TestFetch_ChunkDigestMismatch` was silently not testing what it claimed to.** It only asserted \`err != nil\`, and picked which blob to corrupt via a size heuristic (\`>100 bytes\`). That heuristic isn't reliable — tightening the assertions revealed it was actually corrupting the OCI image index blob, not a chunk blob, which fails store initialization *before* \`Fetch\`'s per-chunk digest loop ever runs. Fixed by resolving the manifest and picking a blob whose \`MediaType\` is \`MediaTypeChunk\` specifically, plus strengthened assertions (\`errors.Is(ErrIntegrity)\`, the per-chunk error-message shape, and — via a \`Progress\` callback — confirming no \`FileDone\` event was ever emitted).
2. **Push partial-failure had zero coverage.** \`TestPushLocalToRemote_PartialFailureDoesNotCommitManifest\` publishes a chunked artifact (config + chunk-index + chunk blobs = multiple separate uploads before the manifest), pushes to a registry that lets the first blob upload succeed and drops the connection on the second, and asserts the manifest is never written. Verified the mock/test can actually distinguish success from failure (a throwaway sanity variant allowing all uploads through confirms the manifest *is* written then).

Part of the cross-repo Go CI guardrail initiative, Bundle 5 follow-up.

Addresses two of the remaining items in #11 (a real registry smoke cycle in CI and skip-tracking annotations remain open there — the smoke-cycle item is being worked in a follow-up PR).

## Test plan
- [x] \`TestFetch_ChunkDigestMismatch\` — 10x repeat run under \`-race\` clean (previously would have silently passed even corrupting the wrong blob)
- [x] New partial-failure test passes; sanity-checked against an all-succeed variant to confirm it's not vacuously true
- [x] \`go test -race ./...\` — full suite passes
- [x] \`gofmt -l\` / \`go vet\` clean

issue.title: feat(ci): wire real registry push/pull smoke cycle via registry:2 service container
issue.body:
## Summary
The full end-to-end cycle `scripts/sorictl-registry-smoke.sh` exercises (metadata init → dataset push → inspect → fetch → byte-equality → overwrite/skip-if-current) existed and worked, but was never invoked by any CI workflow — `test.yml`/`release.yml` only ran `make test`.

Adds a `registry-smoke` job with a `registry:2` Docker service container. This runs on the same `ubuntu-latest` job allocation as everything else — GitHub Actions service containers don't add billed runner time beyond the job's own duration, so this is effectively free. Points `make smoke-cli` (already wired to the smoke script) at `localhost:5000` with `--plain-http`, no live registry credentials needed. Auth-specific behavior (credential forwarding, real cloud registry quirks) stays covered by the existing env-gated integration tests against Harbor/GHCR/ECR — this only adds the missing "does a real push/pull round-trip against an actual OCI registry implementation work" coverage that ran on every PR nowhere before.

Part of the cross-repo Go CI guardrail initiative, Bundle 5 follow-up. Stacked on #13 (branched from it) — the diff will shrink to just this workflow change once #13 merges.

Addresses the CI smoke-cycle item of #11 (skip-tracking annotations remain open there).

## Test plan
- [x] `actionlint` clean on the modified workflow
- [x] `make build-sorictl` succeeds; confirmed `--plain-http` is wired on `dataset push`/`fetch`/`inspect`
- [ ] **Could not fully dry-run locally — no Docker available in this environment.** The underlying push mechanism (`PlainHTTP` via `registryutil.NewRepository`) is the same code path already exercised extensively against local `httptest` servers in #12/#13's new tests, so confidence is high, but this specifically needs to be watched on its first real CI run.
